title: Replicating Apollo Scheming Evals on Open-Weight Models (Llama, Mistral)

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if scheming behaviors emerge in open-weight models accessible to anyone, proliferation risk changes dramatically compared to scheming being frontier-model-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: adapting Apollo's scheming scenarios requires deep understanding of the evaluation methodology. Running 70B models needs high VRAM. Interpreting scheming behaviors requires AI safety domain knowledge beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: 'adapt scenarios to run against' multiple models and sizes is open-ended. Which scenarios transfer and which don't requires iterative exploration. Documentation of results across model families is a broad undertaking.

novelty.reasoning: Apollo Research's original scheming paper (Dec 2024) already tested Llama 3.1 405B alongside frontier models, finding it capable of in-context scheming. However, the paper did not test smaller open-weight models (8B, 70B) or Mistral models. The 'More Capable Models Are Better At In-Context Scheming' follow-up (2025) studied capability scaling but focused on frontier models. No published replication systematically covers smaller Llama variants (8B, 70B) or Mistral family models. The gap is real but narrower than the idea implies since 405B was already tested.

evidence: Meinke et al. Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming. arXiv:2412.04984, Dec 2024.
